svg.text: A6 The foot-closed jig bench: a stop for every placement, no motor (schematic)
Left: the bench seen from the front, treadle under it. Right: the neck at hold, section along the contact. Bottom: what each jig grows into.
toe: <= ~120 N over ~60 mm at 2:1 (calc w2 §5)
loom: far end already in the block
The neck at hold (section along the contact; 1 mm = 60 px; box to the left)
in front of the anvil face (or a relief)
blade 0.10 steel, bare rear face = strand stop + electrode (green)
polyimide on its front face and slot edges: insulated from the box
slot straddles the floor strip; tines stop at its lower face
Room for a brush = transition - blade (0.13-0.15): +0.05 to +0.38 mm (calc w2 §1).
Below ~0.3 mm transition: no blade; locate by the stub's pilot pin, depth by the
camera line. Lift the crimp 1-1.7 mm before drawing it back: the lance meets the
anvil face otherwise. The blade never carries the proof pull (calc w2 §2).
Each jig this week, and what drives it later
Klein in a squeezer (a2c), laser score (b4)
a worm winch on the same cord, or the NEMA 17 pusher (a1, a1b, a2)
the same block and ESP32 run the motors
the same sensors under a motor: force against travel on every crimp
servo or stepper on the lever, leaf kept as the limit; v5's readings logged (a2's pull slot)
a sprung seat takes a contact already on its wire: no blade, single-stage treadle
servo on the lever, or i3's housing press (a2d)
